reasons: Both `addlist` copies (`boltons/dictutils.py` and the private one in `boltons/urlutils.py`) now call `v = list(v)` before the empty check and before the traversal. A one-shot iterator is therefore consumed exactly once. All values are kept in yield order, so the later loop and `values.extend(v)` agree. An empty iterable returns early and does not create the key. Lists, tuples and other sequences behave as before. The change is one line in each of the two source files, with nothing unrelated touched.
